chunks: He would have surely turned us away from our gods if we had not adhered to them." They will know soon who is farther away from the path when they see the punishment!

key_terms.آلِهَتِنَا: our gods (plural of ilah, referring to false deities)

ai.seo_question: What do the polytheists realize in Hell regarding their false gods and their own misguidance?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the subtle interplay between divine grace and human agency, where polytheists acknowledge that their false deities nearly led them astray had they not maintained steadfastness (sabr) in their worship. The concluding rhetorical question emphasizes personal accountability, a core tenet in Shia theology, as the disbelievers realize in Hell that their own choices, rather than external forces, were the primary cause of their deviation. This reflects the concept of 'tawassul' of the idols being ineffective, underscoring the ultimate authority of Allah's decree.
